def: Text in a model's input that is meant to be data but is obeyed as instructions, causing behaviour the operator or user did not intend.
Prompt injection in which a third party plants instructions in content an agent later reads, so the attacker never talks to the system directly.
The combination of access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and a way to communicate externally, which lets an attacker steal data through an agent.
Meta's guideline that within one session an agent should satisfy no more than two of: untrusted input, sensitive access, and the ability to change state or communicate externally.
Sending private data out of a system to a place an attacker can read, for example through a URL, an email or a rendered image.
Hiding malicious instructions in a tool's description, where the model reads them but the approving person usually does not.
A tool server changing a tool's definition after the user approved it, so earlier approval no longer reflects what the model sees.
A malicious tool's description altering how the agent uses a different, trusted tool.
A zero-click prompt injection in Microsoft 365 Copilot (CVE-2025-32711) that leaked data via a crafted email by chaining several bypasses.
Marking untrusted text, for example with delimiters or encoding, so the model can tell which tokens are data.
Training a model to prioritise system instructions over user text and user text over tool output.
A design in which the agent fixes its plan from the trusted request before reading untrusted data, then refuses steps outside the plan.
A defence that extracts control and data flow from the trusted query and uses capabilities to enforce policy at tool-call time.
